note: Complete public scientific-checker bank. Inactive unless SCIBENCH_TRIGGER_LOG is set.

checkers.alarm: max(abs(D@S_solver@D - 2*D)) exceeds 50*eps64*max(nao*cond(S_solver), max|D|**2)
checkers.invariant: D S D == 2 D for the converged density matrix
checkers.observation_point: at kernel()'s return, once scf_conv is True and mo_occ is confirmed closed-shell
checkers.precondition: any converged closed-shell RHF calculation (mo_occ in {0,2} only), any molecule/basis For a symmetry-adapted SCF (hf_symm/uhf_symm classes) the overlap in the law is the block-symmetrised S_blk = sum_ir O_ir (O_ir^T S O_ir) O_ir^T (the metric hf_symm.eig solves against); this differs from the exact overlap when the geometry is accepted as symmetric within symm_geom_tol without being symmetrised. Otherwise S.
checkers.rationale: idempotency under the AO metric is the defining algebraic signature of a valid single-determinant wavefunction; a bug in threading mo_coeff/mo_occ from the eigensolver into make_rdm1 would break this silently
checkers.scientific_quantity: one-particle density matrix of a closed-shell RHF wavefunction
checkers.symbol: kernel (observation point; make_rdm1 is where D is built)

checkers.alarm: abs(trace(D S) - nelectron) exceeds 50*eps64*nao (trace half, all paths); sum(mo_occ) != nelectron exactly (integer half, tol=0, skipped entirely -- mo_occ_sum=None -- when type(mf) is AtomSphAverageRHF) (trace half: tolerance also scales with cond(S))
checkers.invariant: trace(D S) == mol.nelectron (numerical, checked on all paths) and sum(mo_occ) == mol.nelectron (exact integer, checked only on the outer SCF object's own mo_occ, not AtomSphAverageRHF's internal one)
checkers.observation_point: at kernel()'s return, alongside PS-SCF-001
checkers.precondition: any RHF/UHF/ROHF calculation, converged or not, any molecule/basis/charge/spin -- EXCLUDING AtomSphAverageRHF's internal average-of-configuration atomic sub-solve (init_guess='atom'/'huckel' invoke it internally), whose mo_occ is fractional by construction (atom_hf.py's frac_occ, e.g. O 2p: 4/3) and has no integer-valued law to check The sum(mo_occ) half applies only to integer occupations (smeared/fractional occupations are excluded).
checkers.rationale: total electron count is the most basic conserved quantity in electronic structure; mol.nelectron, get_occ's Aufbau filling, and mulliken_pop's AO-integral-based trace are three independently implemented paths that should agree
checkers.scientific_quantity: total electron count, cross-checked via trace(D S) against mol.nelectron and sum(mo_occ) against mol.nelectron

checkers.alarm: max(abs(dip1_au - dip2_au)) of the trace-corrected difference exceeds max(50*eps64*nelectron*(shift + rmax), 100*eps64*E), E = max over x of sum_ij |<i|r_x|j>||D_ji| + shift*sum_ij |S_ij||D_ji| (the absolute magnitude of the two electronic contractions); rmax = largest coordinate of any atom relative to either origin; n_ref = max(nelectron, |tr(DS)|)
checkers.invariant: dip_moment(mol, dm, origin=o1) == dip_moment(mol, dm, origin=o2) for any o1 != o2 (2026-10-09: for a density with tr(D S) != nelectron the exact shift (tr(D S)-nelectron)*(o2-o1) is subtracted before comparing; for an N-electron density this is the unchanged law)
checkers.observation_point: inside dip_moment(), a re-call sanitizer compares against a second call shifted by [0.37, 0, 0] (guarded against infinite recursion via a _scibench_recall kwarg)
checkers.precondition: mol.charge == 0, any molecule/basis/density matrix (an unnormalised density, e.g. the MINAO/VSAP guess with tr(DS)=1.975, is handled by the trace correction in the invariant)
checkers.rationale: users routinely translate geometries before/after a dipole calculation, trusting origin-independence for neutral systems; a violation would indicate the electronic/nuclear origin-dependent terms are inconsistently parametrized
checkers.scientific_quantity: electric dipole moment of a charge-neutral molecule

checkers.alarm: max(abs(C^dagger S_solver C - I)) exceeds 50*eps64*cond(S_solver)
checkers.invariant: C^dagger S C == I for the converged mo_coeff
checkers.observation_point: at kernel()'s return, for any 2D (RHF-shaped) mo_coeff
checkers.precondition: any converged SCF calculation, any molecule/basis (including near-singular S) For a symmetry-adapted SCF the overlap in the law is the block-symmetrised S_solver (see PS-SCF-001); otherwise S.
checkers.rationale: PySCF never itself re-verifies scipy.linalg.eigh(h,s)'s orthonormality contract before handing mo_coeff to every downstream consumer (make_rdm1, get_grad, canonicalize, population analysis)
checkers.scientific_quantity: molecular orbitals from the Roothaan-Hall generalized eigenproblem
checkers.symbol: kernel (observation point; eig() computes the raw eigensolver output)

checkers.alarm: max(abs(D_before - D_after)) exceeds 50*eps_in*nao*cond(S), eps_in = unit roundoff of the coarsest dtype among the input orbitals and the densities (eps64 for float64 orbitals)
checkers.invariant: make_rdm1(canonicalize(mo_coeff,mo_occ)[1], mo_occ) == make_rdm1(mo_coeff, mo_occ)
checkers.observation_point: at canonicalize()'s return, computing make_rdm1 before and after
checkers.precondition: any RHF mo_coeff/mo_occ pair with floating-point orbitals, converged or not, any occupation pattern AND (2026-10-09) occupations inside the open block (all values other than 0 and 2) are equal; hf.canonicalize diagonalises that block as a whole, which changes D when the occupations differ.
checkers.rationale: canonical orbitals are the standard starting point for MP2/CCSD/CASSCF specifically because they are trusted to represent the same physical state; a block-diagonalization bug that mixed an orbital across occupation classes would silently produce a different reference state
checkers.scientific_quantity: one-particle density matrix under a within-subspace orbital rotation

checkers.alarm: abs(trace(dm s) - nelectron) exceeds 50*eps_in*nao*max(1,max|D|) (project=False) or 50*eps_in*nao*4*max(1,max|D|) (project=True), eps_in = unit roundoff of the coarsest dtype among the density matrix and the stored orbitals (eps64 for float64 storage)
checkers.invariant: trace(dm @ get_ovlp(mol)) == mol.nelectron (2026-10-09: S is the target mol's overlap for project=True and the checkpoint molecule's overlap for project=False, the metric in which the reused orbitals are normalised)
checkers.observation_point: at init_guess_by_chkfile()'s return, computing trace(dm @ s) for the target mol, gated on the same-system inertia-moment check
checkers.precondition: any call with a checkpoint from a completed SCF, restoring onto the SAME chemical system (checkpoint's and target mol's moments of inertia agree within 1% relative, the same signal init_guess_by_chkfile itself already computes and warns on for dissimilar geometries) -- basis and/or geometry may still differ; genuinely different molecules (different atoms/composition) are explicitly out of scope The checkpoint's own occupations must sum to the target nelectron.
checkers.rationale: an initial guess with the wrong electron count doesn't just converge slowly -- for the primary project=True different-molecule restart use case, it can start the SCF searching for the wrong physical state entirely
checkers.scientific_quantity: electron count of a checkpoint-projected initial-guess density matrix

checkers.alarm: emp2 exceeds 50*eps64*abs(e_hf)
checkers.invariant: emp2 <= 0 (up to numerical slack)
checkers.observation_point: at kernel()'s return, gated on mp.frozen indicating a canonical reference
checkers.precondition: canonical (frozen in (0, None)) closed-shell RHF reference with an Aufbau ordering: every occupied orbital energy lies below every virtual one (HOMO < LUMO); any molecule/basis
checkers.rationale: for a variational zeroth-order reference, the second-order perturbative correction can only lower the energy; a positive result indicates a sign error in t2/energy denominator construction or a non-variational reference slipping through
checkers.scientific_quantity: second-order Moller-Plesset correlation energy at a canonical RHF reference

checkers.alarm: max(abs(t2 - t2.transpose(1,0,3,2))) exceeds 50*eps64*nao**1.5*max(1,max|t2|)*max(1,max|C|)**4
checkers.invariant: t2[i,j,a,b] == t2[j,i,b,a]
checkers.observation_point: at kernel()'s return, on the t2 actually returned (post any DIIS/reshape in the iterative path)
checkers.precondition: any converged t2 tensor for a closed-shell canonical RHF reference
checkers.rationale: the permutation symmetry follows from indistinguishable-particle exchange, not from any single term's construction; a reshape/DIIS bug could silently break it even though update_amps's own pre-DIIS symmetrization step enforces it locally
checkers.scientific_quantity: MP2 double-excitation amplitude tensor

checkers.alarm: abs(trace(dm1) - nelectron) exceeds 50*eps64*nmo (2026-10-09: tolerance 50*eps_in*nmo*max(1,max|dm1|), eps_in = unit roundoff of the coarsest dtype among dm1 and t2 (eps64 for float64 amplitudes))
checkers.invariant: trace(dm1) == mol.nelectron
checkers.observation_point: at make_rdm1()'s return, after ccsd_rdm._make_rdm1 assembles the full matrix
checkers.precondition: converged MP2 on a closed-shell canonical RHF reference, with_frozen=True (default), ao_repr=False The reference mo_occ sums to mol.nelectron.
checkers.rationale: the MP2 density matrix is used directly for dipole/natural-orbital property calculations that implicitly trust it represents a valid particle-number-conserving one-electron description; the trace-conservation property only emerges once doo/dvv correction blocks combine with the reference core contribution across a module boundary (mp2.py -> cc/ccsd_rdm.py)
checkers.scientific_quantity: MP2 one-particle reduced density matrix (with frozen-core reference contribution)

checkers.alarm: max over MOs of |sum_irrep projection - <mo|S|mo>| / <mo|S|mo> exceeds max(1e-12, 5*eps64*cond(S), 50*eps_in*cond(S) for reduced-precision input, A), eps_in = unit roundoff of the coarsest dtype among the orbitals and the overlap, A = d/lambda_min(S)*(1 + d/lambda_min(S)) with d = ||S - S_blk||_2 when 0 < d <= 1e-4*max(1,||S||_2) and 0 otherwise, S_blk = sum_ir O_ir (O_ir^T S O_ir) O_ir^T the block-symmetrised overlap
checkers.invariant: sum_irrep <mo|P_irrep|mo>_S == <mo|mo>_S for every MO (mol.symm_orb is a complete orthonormal symmetry-adapted basis of the AO space)
checkers.observation_point: inside label_orb_symm(), on the per-irrep projected norms before they are normalised to unit sum
checkers.precondition: any symmetry-enabled calculation (mol.symmetry truthy), any point group/basis, any orbitals (symmetry-pure or not, normalised or not, check True/False)
checkers.rationale: the library already computes and acts on this exact quantity but only via a warn/raise gate at ad hoc constants (1e-9, 1e2x); the common, unremarkable case (largest_norm >= 1-tol) is never separately recorded, so a regression that degrades purity without crossing the raise threshold would be invisible today
checkers.scientific_quantity: completeness of the symmetry-adapted basis: the irrep projections of an MO add up to its overlap norm

checkers.alarm: either exact-integer equality fails (tol=0)
checkers.invariant: sum(mo_occ[0]) + sum(mo_occ[1]) == mol.nelectron and sum(mo_occ[0]) - sum(mo_occ[1]) == mol.spin, both exact
checkers.observation_point: at get_occ()'s return
checkers.precondition: any UHF/UKS calculation, converged or not, any valid (charge, spin) Integer occupations and the molecule's own nelec (no user-assigned mf.nelec, no float_occ/smearing).
checkers.rationale: the UHF-specific sibling of PS-SCF-002; every downstream energy/property implicitly assumes the occupation arrays reflect the requested charge/spin state, and a slicing/indexing bug in Aufbau filling would break this without any single line looking locally wrong
checkers.scientific_quantity: alpha/beta electron counts of an unrestricted calculation

checkers.alarm: max(abs(diag(S) - 1)) exceeds 50*4*eps64 (tolerance 2000*eps64) (2026-10-09: per-AO tolerance max(2000*eps64, 50*eps64*kappa), kappa = cancellation factor sum|w_i w_j s_ij|/|sum w_i w_j s_ij| of the AO's contraction; kappa=1 for ordinary bases)
checkers.invariant: diag(int1e_ovlp) is close to all-ones
checkers.observation_point: at the end of Mole.build(), after basis parsing/normalization completes
checkers.precondition: NORMALIZE_GTO enabled (default), spherical basis (cart=False), shells with l <= 6 and all primitive exponents >= 1e-4 (the range of standard basis sets; outside it the integral kernel's small-prefactor screening drops the normalised self-overlap) and raw contraction coefficients whose normalisation integral max|c|^2 * int r^(2l+2) exp(-2 a_min r^2) dr is a normal float64 with eps headroom (coefficients of order 1e+-150 overflow or go subnormal; basis-set coefficients are 1e-6..1e3) -- Cartesian d-and-higher shells excluded pending a separate confirmation read
checkers.rationale: PySCF computes AO self-overlap-equals-1 twice through genuinely independent mechanisms: analytically in Python at basis-parsing time (_nomalize_contracted_ao's closed-form Gaussian formula) and numerically via the compiled libcint integral evaluator at runtime -- these share no intermediate computation
checkers.scientific_quantity: self-overlap of a normalized contracted Gaussian AO

checkers.alarm: abs(n - trace(dm S)) exceeds 1e-3
checkers.invariant: n (grid-integrated electron count) is close to trace(dm @ S)
checkers.observation_point: inside get_veff(), immediately after ni.nr_rks returns n, gated on grids.level >= default
checkers.precondition: RKS/UKS with any XC functional, hermi != 2, ground-state (2D) density matrix; the grid in use is no coarser than the default (grids.level >= the library's current default level, every explicit atom_grid entry (n_rad, n_ang) at least the default for that element, default or no pruning); and the grid resolves the density: the electron-count error the quadrature itself causes, |tr(D (S_grid - S))| with S_grid = sum_g w_g ao ao^T, is at most a tenth of the alarm tolerance (1e-4)
checkers.rationale: PySCF's own debug log already frames n as 'nelec by numeric integration' implying an expected reference value, but nothing in the code path actually validates it against the analytic trace; a violation beyond grid-quadrature error would indicate a real bug in grid construction/pruning or eval_rho's density evaluation
checkers.scientific_quantity: electron count of a density matrix via real-space grid quadrature vs. analytic AO-metric trace

checkers.alarm: abs(n[0]-trace(dm[0] S)) exceeds 1e-3 or abs(n[1]-trace(dm[1] S)) exceeds 1e-3
checkers.invariant: n[0] close to trace(dm[0] S) and n[1] close to trace(dm[1] S), checked independently per channel
checkers.observation_point: inside get_veff(), immediately after ni.nr_uks returns n, before the NLC branch (if any) reassigns n
checkers.precondition: same as PS-DFT-001 (grid no coarser than the default and resolving each spin density), specialized to a genuine 2-component (dm.ndim==3, dm.shape[0]==2) unrestricted density, gated on the non-NLC-branch n being a length-2 tuple
checkers.rationale: checking each spin channel independently (not just their sum) is necessary to catch a channel-swap or one-sided misattribution bug that a combined check would miss
checkers.scientific_quantity: per-spin-channel electron count of an unrestricted density via grid quadrature vs. analytic trace

checkers.alarm: max(abs(t2 - t2.transpose(1,0,3,2))) exceeds 50*eps64
checkers.invariant: t2[i,j,a,b] == t2[j,i,b,a]
checkers.observation_point: at kernel()'s return, on the fully-converged post-DIIS t2
checkers.precondition: any converged t2 tensor from a closed-shell canonical RHF/RCCSD reference (2D-dtype ndarray t2 with 4 dims -- the plain, non-UCCSD path) that went through at least one update_amps step (max_cycle >= 1)
checkers.rationale: same particle-exchange-symmetric-Hamiltonian origin as PS-MP2-002, now checked at the CCSD tier where the amplitude-to-vector DIIS packing is a distinct, more complex implementation with its own _s4-symmetry-packed variant
checkers.scientific_quantity: CCSD double-excitation amplitude tensor

checkers.alarm: abs(trace(dm1) - nelectron) exceeds 50*eps_in*nmo, eps_in = unit roundoff of the coarsest dtype among dm1 and t1, t2, l1, l2 (eps64 for float64 amplitudes)
checkers.invariant: trace(dm1) == mol.nelectron
checkers.observation_point: at CCSD.make_rdm1()'s return, after ccsd_rdm._make_rdm1 assembles the full matrix
checkers.precondition: converged CCSD with converged lambda-amplitudes, closed-shell canonical RHF reference, with_frozen=True, with_mf=True, ao_repr=False
checkers.rationale: unlike MP2's t2-only density matrix, CCSD's depends jointly on two independently-converged iterative solves (the amplitude equations and the separate Lambda-equation solve); trace conservation is a joint property of both being combined correctly
checkers.scientific_quantity: CCSD one-particle reduced density matrix (built from t1/t2 and lambda-amplitudes)

checkers.alarm: max(abs(rho_from_dm - rho_from_mo)) exceeds 50*eps_in*nao*10*max(1, max|rho|, (max|C_occ|*max|ao|)**2)
checkers.invariant: eval_rho(mol, ao, D) == eval_rho2(mol, ao, C_occ, n_occ) on the same grid batch, where D = C_occ diag(n_occ) C_occ^T is built from the same orbitals that feed eval_rho2
checkers.observation_point: inside rks.py's get_veff(), on a 500-point grid subsample, whenever a matching mo_coeff/mo_occ pair is available
checkers.precondition: a ground-state RKS calculation whose mo_coeff/mo_occ are confirmed (within 1e-8) to reproduce the density matrix dm in use, LDA xctype
checkers.rationale: eval_rho (the function PySCF's production DFT path actually calls) and eval_rho2 share no intermediate computation -- one contracts ao against dm via _dot_ao_dm, the other transforms ao to MO space directly -- making agreement a genuine cross-implementation check
checkers.scientific_quantity: real-space electron density rho(r) via density-matrix contraction vs. MO-coefficient contraction

checkers.alarm: max(abs(D_before - D_after)) exceeds 50*eps_in*nao*cond(S)*max(1,n_macro_iterations), eps_in = unit roundoff of the coarsest dtype among the input orbitals and the density matrices (eps64 for float64 orbitals)
checkers.invariant: the occupied-subspace density matrix is unchanged by localization
checkers.observation_point: at kernel()'s return, computing the density matrix from the original and localized mo_coeff
checkers.precondition: any Boys(mol, mo_coeff).kernel() call on S-orthonormal occupied orbitals, more than 1 orbital
checkers.rationale: localized orbitals are trusted to represent the same electronic state as their originals; the CIAH augmented-Hessian optimizer's accumulated rotation u0 could in principle drift off the unitary manifold across many macro-iterations, a risk surface distinct from PS-SCF-005's single-shot block-diagonalization
checkers.scientific_quantity: one-particle density matrix under Boys/Edmiston/Pipek orbital localization

checkers.alarm: abs(analytic - finite_diff) exceeds 1e-5 Hartree/Bohr
checkers.invariant: grad_elec + grad_nuc is close to (E(x+h) - E(x-h))/(2h), h=1e-4 Angstrom central difference, converted to Hartree/Bohr
checkers.observation_point: NOT a re-call sanitizer in any production hot path -- an explicitly-invoked helper (run_finite_difference_check) since a genuine evaluation requires O(natm) extra full SCF solves per invocation, too expensive to run transparently on every gradient call. Never called from inside PySCF itself.
checkers.precondition: converged RHF at a geometry with a genuine, well-separated HOMO-LUMO gap; opt-in invocation only
checkers.rationale: essentially every geometry optimization/TS search/MD trajectory depends on the analytic gradient being correct; PySCF's own test suite only validates gradients against finite differences in curated unit tests, never as a general runtime property. An early sweep attempt without a unit conversion (angstrom displacement vs. Hartree/Bohr gradient) produced an apparent ~2.5e-2 discrepancy that was purely a units bug in the sweep script, not a real finding -- caught and fixed before deriving the real tolerance below.
checkers.scientific_quantity: analytic RHF nuclear energy gradient vs. central finite-difference derivative of the total energy
checkers.source: pyscf/grad/rhf.py (checker itself in pyscf/_scientific_checkers.py, not wired into any production call site)

checkers.alarm: abs(trace(dm1a) - neleca) exceeds 50*eps64*norb or abs(trace(dm1b) - nelecb) exceeds 50*eps64*norb (2026-10-09: tolerance 50*eps64*norb + 4*eps64*ndet, ndet = number of determinants)
checkers.invariant: trace(dm1a) == neleca and trace(dm1b) == nelecb
checkers.observation_point: at make_rdm1s()'s return, on the module-level function (catches all solver variants that call it, not just the FCISolver.make_rdm1s method wrapper)
checkers.precondition: any FCI vector from direct_spin1/direct_spin0/direct_uhf/direct_spin1_symm/direct_spin0_symm (including the non-Hermitian direct_nosym solver and selected-CI's truncated determinant space, both of which the trace law still covers), any norb, any (neleca, nelecb) with 0<=neleca,nelecb<=norb -- excluding direct_ep.py's electron-phonon-coupled vectors (a different mode/electron indexing convention not confirmed to share this law) The identity is stated for the normalized state: the trace is divided by <c|c>. The CI vector is float64, the only dtype the compiled kernel and direct_spin1.energy accept; other dtypes are read as raw float64 memory and are outside the law.
checkers.rationale: the RDM trace is produced entirely by the compiled libfci string-excitation contraction kernel, a code path that never references the caller-supplied nelec integers in computing matrix elements -- an independently implemented path from the values it must agree with, the FCI-tier analogue of the shipped PS-SCF-002/PS-UHF-002/PS-MP2-003/PS-CC-002 electron-count/RDM-trace family
checkers.scientific_quantity: FCI one-particle reduced density matrix (spin-separated)

checkers.alarm: abs(energy(h1e, eri, fcivec, norb, nelec) + ecore - e) exceeds max(1e-8, 50*eps64*S) + N**2*A Hartree, S = |e|+|e_recontracted|+|ecore|+N*max|h1e|+N^2*max|eri|, A = max pair-swap/index-swap asymmetry of eri
checkers.invariant: energy(h1e, eri, fcivec, norb, nelec) + ecore == e, for each (e, fcivec) pair kernel() returns
checkers.observation_point: inside FCISolver.kernel(), immediately after the Davidson/direct solve returns (e, c), looping over roots when nroots>1
checkers.precondition: any converged FCI calculation, any norb/nelec/spin/symmetry-restricted solver variant, both the default Davidson-iterative branch and the davidson_only=False direct-diagonalization branch, any nroots (checked per returned root) The solver's Hamiltonian contraction is unmodified (no fix_spin_ spin penalty or instance-level operator replacement).
checkers.rationale: kernel()'s solver obtains its eigenvalue from the iteration's own internal Ritz-value/LAPACK bookkeeping and never calls energy() to compute the number it reports; energy() independently reconstructs the 2e contraction and recontracts against the returned fcivec via a structurally different arithmetic path -- a bug in how kernel() threads the final eigenvector out of the solver (stale/wrong-root vector, unconverged intermediate) would desynchronize these
checkers.scientific_quantity: FCI ground-/targeted-root energy (Davidson eigenvalue vs. independently recomputed Rayleigh quotient)

checkers.alarm: abs(trace(dm1) - nelectron) exceeds 50*eps_in*nmo, eps_in = unit roundoff of the coarsest dtype among dm1 and the CI vector (eps64 for float64)
checkers.invariant: trace(dm1) == mol.nelectron
checkers.observation_point: at make_rdm1()'s return, MO-basis case only
checkers.precondition: any converged CISD calculation on a closed-shell canonical RHF reference, any molecule/basis, any frozen-core setting, with_frozen=True (default), ao_repr=False -- excluding ucisd.py/gcisd.py (unrestricted/generalized CISD, which have their own _gamma1_intermediates not covered by this checker) and ao_repr=True (AO-basis trace requires the overlap metric, a different check not this one) The reference mo_occ sums to mol.nelectron.
checkers.rationale: CISD's _gamma1_intermediates builds doo/dov/dvo/dvv from the variational, c0-normalized amplitude triple (c0,c1,c2) -- structurally different arithmetic from CCSD's non-variational t1/t2+l1/l2 combination (PS-CC-002) and MP2's t2-only construction (PS-MP2-003), even though all three feed the same downstream ccsd_rdm._make_rdm1 assembly function; a bug specific to CISD's own amplitude-to-intermediate contraction would not be caught by either sibling checker
checkers.scientific_quantity: CISD one-particle reduced density matrix (MO basis, with frozen-core reference contribution)

checkers.alarm: abs(trace(casdm1) - sum(nelecas)) exceeds 50*eps64*ncas (tolerance max(50*eps64*ncas, 1e-9)) (2026-10-09: tolerance max(50*eps64*ncas, 1e-9, 8*eps64*ndet))
checkers.invariant: trace(casdm1) == sum(nelecas), where casdm1 = fcisolver.make_rdm1(fcivec, ncas, nelecas)
checkers.observation_point: at the module-level kernel()'s return, immediately after the FCI solver returns fcivec
checkers.precondition: any converged or unconverged CASCI/CASSCF calculation, RHF- or ROHF-based (spin-restricted-orbital) reference, single-state (not state-averaged -- list/tuple ci is explicitly skipped, matching the state-average carve-out) -- excluding UHF-based CASSCF/CASCI (umc1step.py/ucasci.py use a per-spin (ncore_a, ncore_b) bookkeeping convention not covered by this checker)
checkers.rationale: ncore/nelecas are set once at CASCI/CASSCF construction (often directly by the user) and never algebraically re-derived from the active-space FCI solve; casdm1's trace is produced entirely by the FCI solver's own RDM machinery (PS-FCI-001's law, one layer up), which knows nothing about ncore -- a bug in how the active-space problem is set up for the wrong electron count would not be caught by either function's own code. NOTE: the companion setup-time integer identity 2*ncore+sum(nelecas)==mol.nelectron was investigated at Step 4 and found to already be a hard Python `assert` inside CASBase.check_sanity() (called unconditionally at the top of every kernel()) -- re-observing it as a silent trigger would only restate an invariant the library already enforces by crashing, not a silently-unguarded state (SANITIZER.md 5.1), so only the genuinely unguarded numerical half ships
checkers.scientific_quantity: CASCI/CASSCF active-space electron count (FCI-solver RDM trace vs. the nelecas set at construction)

checkers.alarm: max(abs(D_before - D_after)) exceeds 50*eps_in*nao*cond(S), eps_in = unit roundoff of the coarsest dtype among the input orbitals, the CI vector and the densities (eps64 for float64) (2026-10-09: when cas_natorb=True the tolerance is increased by 2*sum(deviation of folded occupations)*max(1,max|C|^2))
checkers.invariant: total density matrix (2*mocore@mocore.T + mocas@casdm1@mocas.T) is unchanged by canonicalize()
checkers.observation_point: a re-call sanitizer wrapping canonicalize(), computing the total density matrix from the (mo_coeff, ci) pair before the call and from (mo_coeff1, ci) after
checkers.precondition: any single-state (non-state-averaged) CASCI/CASSCF canonicalize() call with floating-point mo_coeff, sort True/False, cas_natorb True/False, RHF-based (restricted-orbital) reference -- excluding UHF-based CASSCF (independent alpha/beta rotations, a different bookkeeping convention) AND (2026-10-09) the density invariance is exact only up to the deliberate folding of active natural orbitals with occupation within casci.FRAC_OCC_THRESHOLD (1e-6) of 0 or 2 into core/virtual space (cas_natorb=True, pyscf issue 1041).
checkers.rationale: unlike the shipped PS-SCF-005/PS-LO-001 (a single orbital rotation at fixed occupation), CASSCF canonicalize() with cas_natorb=True is a simultaneous, jointly-consistent pair of transformations: an active-space orbital rotation (from diagonalizing casdm1) and a CI-vector transformation that must use the identical rotation matrix to stay consistent -- a cross-object consistency law with no molecular-RHF or Boys-localization precedent. Step 4 found that when cas_natorb=False (the default), canonicalize() does not rotate the active block or touch the CI vector at all, so the interesting risk surface is specifically cas_natorb=True's joint rotation (including its near-0/near-2-occupation re-canonicalization sub-branch, which re-solves the CI vector from scratch via a fresh FCI kernel call rather than transform_ci_for_orbital_rotation) -- both settings are included in the precondition and both were empirically exercised
checkers.scientific_quantity: CASCI/CASSCF total (core+active) one-particle density matrix under canonicalization

checkers.alarm: abs(sum(noons) - nelectron) exceeds 50*eps_in*cond(S)*max(1,nelectron)*max(1,max|noons|)*max(1,max|D|) (sum half, any method); max(-noons.min(), noons.max()-2) exceeds 50*eps_in*cond(S)*max(1,max|D|) + ||D||_2*||S - S_solver||_2 (bound half, SCF-level only)
checkers.invariant: sum(noons) == mol.nelectron (any method); each noon in [0,2] (SCF-level references only)
checkers.observation_point: at make_natural_orbitals()'s return, after the scipy.linalg.eigh(A, b=S) generalized eigendecomposition
checkers.precondition: any method_obj with floating-point mo_coeff and a working make_rdm1(ao_repr=True) (RHF/UHF/ROHF/MP2/CCSD/CASSCF/CISD reference objects, both the spin-traced 2D and spin-separated tuple rdm1 branches) for the sum-conservation half; SCF-level (RHF/UHF/ROHF) reference objects only for the individual-NOON [0,2]-bound half, since only a genuine single-determinant density matrix is guaranteed N-representable by construction -- correlated methods' approximate density matrices are explicitly excluded from the bound half (mp2.py's own make_rdm1 docstring flags its output as an approximation, not rigorously N-representable) (2026-10-09: the SCF-level classification is made on the object passed to make_natural_orbitals, not on its _scf reference; MP2/CC/CAS objects were wrongly treated as SCF-level)
checkers.rationale: this is a third, structurally distinct computational route to the electron count beyond the shipped bank's direct AO-metric trace (PS-SCF-002) and grid-quadrature (PS-DFT-001) routes -- a generalized eigendecomposition via LAPACK, an entirely different numerical algorithm whose correctness is not implied by the input density matrix's own trace already being correct (a correct Dm fed through a buggy or mismatched-basis generalized-eigenproblem call would produce eigenvalues that do not sum to the right total even though Dm's own trace is fine)
checkers.scientific_quantity: natural-orbital occupation numbers (generalized-eigenproblem eigenvalues of the AO-metric-transformed density matrix)

checkers.alarm: any of the 3 permutation differences exceeds 50*eps64*nmo**1.5*max(cond(C)**2, max|C|**4)*max(1, max|eri_mo|, max|eri_ao|)
checkers.invariant: eri[i,j,k,l] == eri[j,i,k,l] == eri[i,j,l,k] == eri[k,l,i,j] (the 3 independent constraints implying full 8-fold symmetry for this same-orbital-set real case)
checkers.observation_point: at general()'s return, when all four orbital coefficient arguments are literally the same array and compact=False
checkers.precondition: any ao2mo.incore.general(eri_ao, mo_coeffs, compact=False) call (via full() or directly) with all four mo_coeffs identical (the same array object, not merely equal-valued), any real (non-complex) orbital coefficient matrix, any nao, any nmo<=nao -- excluding mixed orbital sets (general()'s own docstring states mixed sets have at most 4-fold symmetry) and complex orbitals (the function already raises NotImplementedError for these)
checkers.rationale: ao2mo.incore's compiled _ao2mo.nr_e2 kernel performs two sequential half-transforms (half_e1 then nr_e2), not a single symmetric operation -- nothing in the two-pass code structurally guarantees the composed result preserves the AO integral's full 8-fold symmetry, one layer upstream of the shipped PS-MP2-002/PS-CC-001 amplitude-symmetry checks. DESIGN CORRECTION (2026-09-23, independent re-verification): ao2mo.incore.general() has no access to the AO overlap S, so the conditioning term cannot literally be cond(S) as first sketched -- the checker call site passes cond(mo_coeffs[0])**2 instead. This is not an approximation: for S-orthonormal RHF orbitals (C^dagger S C = I), cond(S) == cond(C)**2 exactly, confirmed empirically (ratio within 1e-9 relative across a 4-order-of-magnitude range of cond(S)).
checkers.scientific_quantity: same-orbital-set MO-transformed two-electron integral tensor (8-fold permutation symmetry)

checkers.alarm: epcm exceeds max(50*eps64*abs(epcm), 1e-9 Ha)
checkers.invariant: epcm <= 0 for eps>1
checkers.observation_point: at _get_vind()'s return, in both ddCOSMO (domain-decomposition spherical-harmonic expansion) and PCM (self-consistent-reaction-field boundary elements)
checkers.precondition: any DDCOSMO/PCM _get_vind(dm) call with eps>1 (physically realistic solvent dielectric) and any charge distribution dm (ground-state, perturbed or excited-state density; the sign law is a property of linear dielectric response). The conductor-limit sentinels (ddCOSMO eps<=0, PCM eps==inf) are excluded. For ddCOSMO the expansion is resolved: lmax >= 4 and the Lebedev angular quadrature has at least (lmax+1)^2 points per sphere (a smaller quadrature cannot resolve the harmonic basis and the discretized operator is then not negative-definite), and the volume grid resolves the solute density: the count error |tr(D (S_grid - S))| is at most 1e-3*max(1, N) (an unresolved density makes the grid charge and the analytic potential differ, so the energy is not a definite quadratic form).
checkers.rationale: epcm's sign is not locally forced by the one-line f_epsilon*<psi,Xvec> (ddCOSMO) or 0.5*dot(q_sym,v_grids) (PCM) expression -- both inner products are the output of a separate linear solve over a discretized dielectric-boundary operator (Lmat, or K/R); whether the result comes out with the physically-required sign depends on that operator being correctly assembled, not on the final multiplication. The induced reaction-field polarization always opposes and partially cancels the solute's own field for a passive/dissipative dielectric response, a standard electrostatics theorem
checkers.scientific_quantity: continuum-solvation (dielectric reaction-field) free energy

checkers.alarm: max(abs(b - b_ref)) exceeds 50*eps64*cond(a)*max(abs(b_ref)), where b_ref is a from-scratch cross-product/triple-product re-derivation of b (not the numpy.linalg.inv call the function under test uses)
checkers.invariant: a_i . b_j == norm_to * delta_ij
checkers.observation_point: inside reciprocal_vectors(), immediately after computing b via the production matrix-inverse formula
checkers.precondition: any Cell with dimension==3 and a non-degenerate lattice (vol>0); any norm_to (the duality constant is parametrized by norm_to, not hardcoded to 2*pi)
checkers.rationale: reciprocal_vectors() computes b via a direct matrix inverse (b = norm_to*inv(a.T)); Step 4 found this differs from the scan candidate's assumed cross-product implementation (the docstring states the cross-product formula but the actual code is a matrix inverse) -- to keep the checker's own reference computation genuinely independent, it re-derives b from scratch via the cross-product/triple-product formula the docstring states, a structurally different numerical routine from the production code's LAPACK matrix inverse. Every reciprocal-space quantity in the PBC code (k-point grids, Gv plane-wave vectors, Ewald summation, density fitting) is built from this function's output
checkers.scientific_quantity: reciprocal lattice vectors (duality relation with the real-space lattice vectors)

checkers.alarm: abs(e_direct - e_pme) exceeds 1e-6*max(abs(e_direct), eta/sqrt(pi)*sum(Z^2), 1e-8), eta = Ewald exponent, Z = atomic charges of the cell
checkers.invariant: Cell.ewald()'s direct real+reciprocal-space summation agrees with particle_mesh_ewald()'s FFT/B-spline approximation, within PME's own interpolation/grid discretization error
checkers.observation_point: inside ewald(), when the PME branch is taken: a re-call sanitizer additionally computes the direct-summation path (temporarily overriding use_particle_mesh_ewald=False) and compares
checkers.precondition: any Cell with dimension==3, use_particle_mesh_ewald=True, any lattice, any nonzero-charge atom configuration, any ew_eta/ew_cut/interpolation order -- the law holds for any cell where both methods are computable, not narrowed to large-cell-only use cases AND (2026-10-09) the real-space Ewald sum is converged: erfc(ew_eta*ew_cut) <= 1e-7 (default parameters satisfy this; the two paths truncate the real-space sum differently, shell vs sphere) and cell.precision <= 1e-6 (the mesh is sized from cell.precision, so a looser user setting legitimately allows a PME deviation of that size).
checkers.rationale: Step 4 found particle_mesh_ewald() actually shares the real-space (ewovrl, via the identical compiled _get_ewald_direct kernel) and self-energy (ewself, identical closed-form expression) terms bit-for-bit with the direct path -- a stronger shared-arithmetic situation than the scan candidate assumed; only the reciprocal-space term (ewg, a B-spline/FFT convolution vs. a direct Gv-grid sum) genuinely differs, cleanly isolating any disagreement to a genuine discretization-error comparison rather than roundoff. A genuine correctness bug in either algorithm's distinct reciprocal-space construction would not be locally visible from either function's own code
checkers.scientific_quantity: electrostatic (Madelung) lattice energy, computed via two structurally different Ewald-summation algorithms

checkers.alarm: sum_k(mo_occ_kpts[k].sum()) != cell.tot_electrons(nkpts) (exact integer, tol=0)
checkers.invariant: sum_k(mo_occ_kpts[k].sum()) == cell.tot_electrons(nkpts)
checkers.observation_point: at get_occ()'s return
checkers.precondition: any converged or unconverged KRHF calculation, any cell/basis/k-mesh size and shape, including partially-filled/near-degenerate-HOMO-LUMO (metallic) systems -- excluding smearing-decorated KSCF objects (a materially different, temperature-dependent fractional-occupation assignment mechanism)
checkers.rationale: get_occ() pools the spectrum across ALL sampled k-points via a single sort, finds one shared Fermi level, then applies that threshold INDEPENDENTLY to each k-point's own spectrum -- occupation counts may differ from k-point to k-point (a metal's band crossing the Fermi level at different points in the Brillouin zone is the physically expected case this mechanism exists to handle), so the conserved quantity is the SUM over k-points, not a per-k-point count; no line in get_occ re-verifies that summing mo_occ_kpts back up actually reproduces tot_electrons(nkpts) after the per-k thresholding step -- a k-mesh bookkeeping bug (e.g. an nkpts mismatch between the two independently-computed forms it appears in) would not be locally visible
checkers.scientific_quantity: k-point-sampled RHF total electron count (pooled-spectrum-then-per-k-threshold occupation, summed over the k-mesh)

checkers.alarm: either sum differs from its expected nocc (exact integer, tol=0)
checkers.invariant: sum_k(mo_occ_kpts[0][k].sum()) == nocc_a and sum_k(mo_occ_kpts[1][k].sum()) == nocc_b, where (nocc_a, nocc_b) = mf.nelec (already the k-mesh-summed per-spin total, not a per-cell count)
checkers.observation_point: at get_occ()'s return
checkers.precondition: any converged or unconverged KUHF calculation, any cell/basis/k-mesh, any (charge, spin) combination compatible with non-negative integer nocc_a/nocc_b, including nocc_b==0 (fully spin-polarized references, handled by the code's own zero-occupation branch) -- excluding smearing-decorated KUHF objects
checkers.rationale: exercises two composed risk surfaces neither PS-PBC-004 nor the shipped molecular PS-UHF-002 exercises alone: the pooled-spectrum-then-per-k mechanism (new to the k-point case) AND the alpha/beta bookkeeping split (new to the unrestricted case), together in one function neither parent checker's code path ever calls. Step 4 found mf.nelec is already the k-mesh-summed total (derived from cell.tot_electrons(nkpts)), correcting the scan candidate's alarm formula (which incorrectly proposed an extra nkpts multiplicative factor)
checkers.scientific_quantity: k-point-sampled UHF per-spin electron count (pooled-spectrum-then-per-k-threshold occupation, summed over the k-mesh, per spin channel)

checkers.alarm: aspect_ratio (passed by the call site, None if unavailable) <= 3.0 or unknown, AND ecell.ewald() exceeds 50*eps64*max(abs(ecell.ewald()), 1e-8)
checkers.invariant: ecell.ewald() <= 0 (the probe-charge self-energy is stabilizing for a reasonably-shaped 3D lattice, the crystal-electrostatics analogue of the shipped PS-SOLV-001's continuum-dielectric sign theorem)
checkers.observation_point: inside madelung(), immediately after ecell.ewald() is computed, before the -2x rescale is applied and returned
checkers.precondition: any Cell with dimension==3, omega==0 (full-range Coulomb; the omega!=0 range-separated branch is a different physical partial-range quantity, explicitly out of scope), any Monkhorst-Pack mesh size including Nk=(1,1,1) -- AND (added 2026-09-23, see fix note below) the Nk-scaled ecell's own lattice-vector-length aspect ratio max(|a_i|)/min(|a_i|) <= 3.0. Cells built as a large-vacuum-padded 3D box around a short periodic axis to emulate a lower-dimensional system (the standard workaround when a code path requires dimension>1) fall outside this precondition. (2026-10-09: the aspect ratio is measured on a Minkowski-style reduced basis of ecell's lattice, not on the supplied vectors; a skew choice of basis for an elongated lattice made the supplied-vector ratio 1.02 instead of 5.9)
checkers.rationale: Step 4 finding: the scan candidate's originally-proposed observation point (madelung()'s own OUTPUT) is NOT reliably negative -- empirically found POSITIVE in every trial of a 4-lattice sweep, because the -2x convention factor (used to convert the raw self-energy into the exact-exchange finite-size-correction magnitude) flips the sign of the actually-well-understood physical quantity. This is a Step 4 correction to the candidate, not a rejection of the underlying law: the genuinely well-understood, textbook-confirmable sign statement is about ecell.ewald() itself, observed at the earlier point inside madelung() before the sign-flipping rescale. ecell.ewald()'s own three-term sum (real-space erfc sum, self-energy, reciprocal-space Gv-grid sum) has a documented history of subtle sign/factor errors (the function's own inline comment flags a textbook reference formula as 'off by a factor of 2, the exponent is wrong ... and the square is in the wrong place'), so this is not an algebraically-guaranteed sign
checkers.scientific_quantity: electrostatic self-energy of a single probe unit point charge and its periodic images in a neutralizing background (crystal-lattice Ewald summation), observed before madelung()'s -2x exact-exchange-convention rescale

checkers.alarm: emp2 exceeds 50*eps64*abs(e_hf)*nkpts
checkers.invariant: emp2 <= 0
checkers.observation_point: at kernel()'s return, gated on mp.frozen indicating a canonical reference and a nonzero gap confirmed at every sampled k-point
checkers.precondition: any closed-shell canonical KRHF reference with a nonzero band gap at every sampled k-point, both the density-fitted (with_df_ints=True, default when mf.with_df is GDF) and exact-integral (with_df_ints=False) contraction paths -- excluding kmp2_ksymm.py (k-point-symmetry-adapted variant, a separate module with an unverified amplitude/energy accumulation structure)
checkers.rationale: kmp2.kernel() is fully independent code from molecular mp2.py -- its own triple-k-point (ki,kj,ka->kb via kconserv) summation structure, its own DF or exact-integral contraction path, and its own 1/nkpts energy normalization, with no molecular-code analog; the same variational-reference argument as the shipped PS-MP2-001 extends to a Brillouin-zone sum of individually non-positive per-k-triple contributions, and a sign/contraction-index bug specific to the k-point triple-loop structure would be a genuinely different, PBC-specific risk surface PS-MP2-001's checker never exercises
checkers.scientific_quantity: second-order Moller-Plesset correlation energy at a canonical k-point-sampled RHF reference

checkers.alarm: max over all (ki,kj,ka) triples of abs(t2[ki,kj,ka] - t2[kj,ki,kb].transpose(1,0,3,2)) exceeds 50*eps64
checkers.invariant: t2[ki,kj,ka][i,j,a,b] == t2[kj,ki,kb][j,i,b,a], where kb = kconserv[ki,ka,kj] (the k-point generalization of the shipped PS-MP2-002/PS-CC-001 orbital-only permutation law)
checkers.observation_point: at update_amps()'s return, on the fully-updated t2new (after the function's own internal symmetrization step)
checkers.precondition: any t2 tensor from update_amps for a closed-shell canonical KRHF/KRCCSD reference, any cell/basis/k-mesh size, any occupied/virtual space including frozen-core-reduced spaces, both DF and exact-integral construction paths (the symmetrization step operates on t2new downstream of wherever the integrals came from) -- excluding kccsd_rhf_ksymm.py (k-point-symmetry-adapted variant, not verified to share this exact structure)
checkers.rationale: update_amps' own explicit t2new[kj,ki,kb] += t2new_tmp.transpose(1,0,3,2) symmetrization step is evidence the law must hold by design; this checker verifies it SURVIVES at the function's own return across the k-point DIIS vectorization, exactly as the shipped PS-CC-001 verifies molecular t2 survives its DIIS round trip -- a k-point-specific reshape/indexing bug in how the three k-point dimensions are flattened into and out of the DIIS vector (a risk surface with no molecular-code analog, since a molecular calculation has only one 'k-point') would not be caught by PS-CC-001, which never calls this function
checkers.scientific_quantity: k-point-sampled CCSD double-excitation amplitude tensor (joint k-point/orbital-index permutation symmetry)

checkers.alarm: abs(e.imag) exceeds 1e-6 Hartree, for a confirmed time-reversal-symmetric mesh only
checkers.invariant: abs(e.imag) is negligible for a time-reversal-symmetric mesh
checkers.observation_point: inside energy(), at the existing abs(e.imag)>1e-4 warn check, independent of whether that warn condition fires
checkers.precondition: any converged KRCCSD calculation on a k-mesh confirmed closed under k -> -k (modulo a reciprocal lattice vector, checked directly rather than inferred from how the mesh was constructed) for a real (non-complex, no spin-orbit/magnetic-field term) Hamiltonian -- excluding deliberately non-time-reversal-symmetric or shifted k-meshes (no general theorem forces e.imag->0 for such a mesh; the physical cancellation this law relies on requires the mesh symmetry itself)
checkers.rationale: energy()'s own logger.warn(...) at abs(e.imag)>1e-4 already identifies e.imag as diagnostically meaningful but never records the passing case for audit purposes, and the threshold reads as an unexamined round constant -- the same situation that motivated the shipped PS-SYM-001. The imaginary part is a GLOBAL, mesh-level cancellation property (pairing k and -k contributions across the entire nkpts^3-term triple loop), not locally guaranteed by any single line; a genuine defect in the k-point pairing/kconserv bookkeeping would break the k/-k cancellation without any single line looking locally wrong
checkers.scientific_quantity: k-point-sampled CCSD correlation energy (imaginary part on a time-reversal-symmetric k-mesh)
